newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: SOCCER-TEENAGE GOALIE BIDS FOR TOP SPOT AFTER HEROIC DISPLAY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-TEENAGE GOALIE BIDS FOR TOP SPOT AFTER HEROIC DISPLAY.

text.p: The footballing world of young reserve goalkeeper Alexander Manninger was transformed this week through another player's misfortune.
Manninger, a 19-year-old reserve goalkeeper at Casino Graz, expected to be on the bench when his side travelled to Inter-Milan for a UEFA Cup match at the daunting San Siro Stadium.
But shortly before kick-off Manninger was told he was playing in place of number one 'keeper Franz Almer, who had fallen ill with a stomach infection and high fever.

Instead of being overawed by the occasion, Manninger played brilliantly, kept Graz in the game with a series of outstanding saves and is now poised to keep the number one shirt when Graz face his former club SV Salzburg on Saturday.
Although Graz lost 1-0 to Inter, coach August Starek praised the youngster's performance afterwards.
"Manninger saved us in many tricky situations against Inter," said Starek. "The goal was unfortunate but definitely not his fault. There was little he could have done to prevent it."

Manninger, Austria's under-21 goalkeeper, is expected to keep his place for Saturday's first division match against his former club, the current league leaders SV Salzburg, even though Almer is now fit again.
Manninger's last league appearance was on June 1, when he played for Salzburg and kept a clean sheet in a 4-0 win over Vorwaerts Steyr.
Manninger might not be the only new face in the Graz lineup as Croatian midfielder Stipe Brnas, is expected to make his debut as well.

Brnas, 27, who previously played for Croatian first division club Sisak, signed a four-year contract with the club this week, but is ineligible to play against Inter in the second leg of their UEFA Cup second round tie.
